changelog: 1. "Jump to Latest" removed -- button and its handler both gone. A replay whose cursor is already the latest visible point had nothing to jump to. advance() is Next Bar only now (always exactly one step); the old jump_to_latest/MAX_JUMP_BARS batch-catch-up logic is removed from BacktestController entirely, not just hidden from the UI.

2. Adaptive replay stepping: one click now advances by the FINER of (viewed timeframe, session's own replay timeframe), not always the session's nominal replay timeframe. Viewing 15m while replaying a nominally 1H session steps 15 minutes per click; viewing 4H/1D while replaying 1H still steps 1H per click, letting the coarser candle visibly build in front of the user (4 clicks for one 4H bar, 24 for one daily bar) -- confirmed this includes the 1D case specifically, which previously served the whole stored daily candle in one tick. New backtest_sessions.cursor_step_tf column records which resolution the most recently revealed bar actually came from (the session's replay_timeframe alone was no longer enough to answer that, once stepping can go finer than it) -- get_backtest_candles' no-lookahead ceiling, and the market-fill/close price lookup (currentBar(), now always reading the 15m series at the exact cursor position, which is always resolvable regardless of what resolution the last step used), both use it. Rewind (Prev Bar) uses the same adaptive step and unchanged v3.20.10 rewind semantics (state after the new cursor undone, trades flagged rewound, confirmation when trades are affected). Play auto-advances at this same adaptive step, so one 'tick' of Play always means the same thing regardless of speed -- only how FAST it repeats changes, never how far each repetition goes. The step size is now always shown in the controls bar ('Step: <tf>'), computed identically on the client (for display) and the server (for actual enforcement) from the same two inputs.

get_backtest_candles' synthesis decision (whether the currently-displayed timeframe's own bar needs the partial-candle treatment) is now a direct question -- does the no-lookahead ceiling fall strictly before that bar's own end? -- rather than v3.20.10's proxy comparison between two timeframes' durations, since cursor_step_tf can now be finer than replay_timeframe while the display timeframe sits anywhere relative to either. The elapsed-portion aggregation itself now always reads real 15m candles (the finest and always-available series) rather than the session's own replay-timeframe ones, which composes correctly with adaptive stepping without needing a separate code path for it.

3. Refreshing the page (or following a copied link, or using the browser's back/forward buttons) now restores the same page -- and, in Backtesting, the same open session -- instead of always landing back on the dashboard. A minimal hash-based router (#<page> or #<page>:<param>, e.g. #backtest:42) was added to js/app.js, app-wide: every showPage() call persists to the URL, and a hashchange listener restores it, guarded against re-triggering a redundant reload from a hash change the app just made itself. No server-side routing changes.

Verification note: the browser-rendered adaptive-stepping/chart behavior across timeframes could not be exercised from this environment -- confirmed instead by lint and hand-traced boundary arithmetic (including the 1D-in-one-tick scenario specifically named in the brief). Please run the ticket's own verification (view 15m/4H/1D on a 1H session and confirm the stated click counts, no lookahead on any timeframe, and a mid-session refresh restoring the same session/timeframe) after deploying.
release_notes: MANUAL DB STEP REQUIRED, not run by this release: after Update Now, run migrate.php?mode=status then mode=run to apply migrations/2026_09_26_0002_add_backtest_cursor_step_tf.sql (adds backtest_sessions.cursor_step_tf, backfilled to each existing row's own replay_timeframe). Uses the information_schema-check + PREPARE/EXECUTE pattern for the ADD COLUMN (MySQL 8.4-safe); the UPDATE and MODIFY COLUMN statements need no such guard (both are naturally idempotent). Per instruction, migrations were NOT run and nothing was deployed as part of this turn.
